title: Premature Read-Copy-Update (RCU) on High-Write Workloads
pattern: Replacing standard locks with read-copy-update (RCU) or deferred hazard-pointer synchronization schemes on a data structure that experiences frequent updates.
why_bad: RCU is optimized exclusively for read-mostly scenarios. In write-heavy workloads, the overhead of allocating new versions of objects, keeping track of grace periods, and executing deferred garbage collection destroys write performance and leads to high memory overhead [17, 61, 142].
detection: Use of complex deferred-free, grace-period monitoring, or double-pointer swap algorithms for collections or variables that undergo frequent modifications (high write-to-read ratio).
counterexample: Read-mostly directories (such as routing tables or configuration parameters) where updates occur less than 1% of the time. `Contextual`.
fix: Use standard locks (`std::sync::RwLock` or `Mutex`) that perform extremely well when updates are common.
